paragraphs: Daxko sells membership management software and built-in payments to health and wellness organizations. Its original and core market is nonprofit community organizations: YMCAs, Boys & Girls Clubs, JCCs and community centers. For them it offers Daxko Operations and Daxko Core, which cover membership, program and child care registration, scheduling, billing, point-of-sale, facility access and fundraising, plus Daxko Engage and Engage Pro for member engagement and retention. Over time it has added a large portfolio for private fitness operators. Club Automation and CSI serve health clubs and multipurpose facilities. Zen Planner and SugarWOD serve boutique studios, CrossFit-style gyms and martial arts schools. Motionsoft, Daxko Exercise and FitnessForce serve multi-location and franchise operators, with FitnessForce built for international markets. Other add-ons include Daxko Payments, GroupEx Pro for class scheduling, Playerspace for league management, Elevate Wellness, revenue recovery services, and newer AI products (a FrontDesk assistant, AI-built websites and member analytics).

Daxko replaces an operator's separate systems for member records, billing, class and program scheduling, check-in and marketing with one system of record. For a YMCA, that means members join, register for programs, book classes and pay online, and the front desk handles check-in, point-of-sale and billing in the same platform. Finance teams get the accounting and fundraising tools nonprofits need. Payments are a large part of the business model: Daxko processes the recurring dues and fees that run through the software, and its revenue recovery service chases failed payments. The company says its software runs in about 19,000 fitness and wellness facilities in 55 countries, serving more than 25 million members. It sells directly, and I found no government contract vehicles. One caveat for your list: Daxko's buyers are nonprofits and private gyms, not government agencies, so it sits next to govtech rather than in it. Its main public-sector overlap is municipal rec centers that run like YMCAs.

Daxko was founded in 1998 and is headquartered at 600 University Park Place in Birmingham, Alabama, with a second hub in Denver. Pamlico Capital backed it earlier and sold to GI Partners in September 2016, when Daxko had about 1,200 customers and 195 employees. In October 2021, Genstar Capital joined GI Partners as a co-investor in a recapitalization meant to fund product development, sales and acquisitions. Much of the current brand lineup came from that acquisition strategy.
